*Aflac Donates Comforting robotic companions to pediatric cancer and blood disorder patients*


INDIANAPOLIS


, Oct. 28, 2026


/[PRNewswire](http://www.prnewswire.com/) / -- Children receiving care for cancer and blood disorders at Riley Hospital for Children in Indianapolis have a new companion to help bring comfort and joy throughout their treatment journeys.[Aflac Incorporated](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4807019-1&h=1325608313&u=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.aflac.com%2F&a=Aflac+Incorporated) , the leading provider of supplemental health insurance in the U.S1, delivered 40 My Special Aflac Ducks® Tuesday.


Riley Hospital for Children has been supported for more than 100 years by[Riley Children's Foundation](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4807019-1&h=1570346070&u=https%3A%2F%2Frileykids.org%2F&a=Riley+Children%27s+Foundation) . Their fundraising efforts have contributed to Riley Children's Health and Riley-affiliated pediatric research programs at Indiana University School of Medicine, enabling care for more than 300,000 patients each year in Indiana as the state's only nationally-ranked hospital.


"Children facing cancer and blood disorders show remarkable courage every day, and we are glad to offer them a bit of help to make difficult moments a little easier, which is the overriding purpose of *My Special Aflac Duck* ," said Ines Rodriguez Gutzmer, Aflac senior vice president and chief communications officer. "We are honored to partner with Riley Hospital for Children and grateful for the compassionate care its team provides to children and families every day across Indiana."


As part of a fun-filled day, patients and families were provided with a demonstration of *My Special Aflac Duck* , which includes accessories like RFID emoji cards that promote communication and medical play. Additionally, an engaging app enables kids to actively participate in a variety of activities. Each child also took part in a scavenger hunt around the hospital, eventually finding their way to tasty treats before receiving their very own *My Special Aflac Duck* .


Designed in consultation with more than 100 children, families and medical professionals in partnership with[Empath Labs](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4807019-1&h=2505307510&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.empathlabs.com%2F&a=Empath+Labs) , *My Special Aflac Duck* features lifelike movement and interactive tools that support children throughout their treatment. In 2024,[a three-year clinical study](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4807019-1&h=2609050544&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.choa.org%2Fabout-us%2Fnewsroom%2Freduction-in-anxiety-in-cancer-patients-using-the-my-special-aflac-duck&a=a+three-year+clinical+study) conducted at 8 hospitals across the United States with 160 patients, found evidence suggesting that pediatric patients who received *My Special Aflac Duck* experienced reductions in treatment-related distress and anxiety, while parents and caregivers also reported positive benefits. The award-winning companion was named one of TIME magazine's Best Inventions of 2018 and earned Best in Show honors at CES 2018 and South by Southwest 2019.


"We are grateful to Aflac for its commitment to supporting children and families facing cancer and blood disorders," said Courtney Roberts, president and CEO at Riley Children's Foundation. "Innovative resources like *My Special Aflac Duck* help us care for the whole child while bringing moments of comfort, connection and play during challenging times. We're thankful for Aflac's partnership and the positive impact it will have on the children and families we serve."


Since its debut, Aflac has delivered more than 48,000 *My Special Aflac Ducks* free of charge, to children facing cancer and blood disorders in the United States, Japan and Northern Ireland. The program is a hallmark of Aflac's longstanding commitment to children with pediatric cancer and blood disorders, including a recently achieved milestone of contributing more than $200 million toward research, treatment and support programs over the past three decades.


Health care providers, support organizations and families can order a *My Special Aflac Duck* free of charge for children ages 3 and older who have been diagnosed with cancer or sickle cell disease at[MySpecialAflacDuck.com](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4807019-1&h=1108122991&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.aflacchildhoodcancer.org%2F&a=MySpecialAflacDuck.com) .
